## Emma's school play rehearsals (keywords: Emma, school play, rehearsal, East Janethaven Theater, November 25)

- November 20, 2024: user is stressed about Emma's school play rehearsals starting November 25, 2024 (a Monday).
- User has scheduled to attend all 5 evening rehearsals at East Janethaven Theater (user's account).
- Not yet on file: exact rehearsal dates and start/end times, time zone, the user's work hours, and whether other family members need coverage.
- Requested: help planning the schedule around the rehearsals.
- November 20, 2024 (follow-up): user has a "time anchor" of Nov 20, 2024 and wants advice on balancing family support (attending rehearsals) with personal needs. Prioritization advice given: fixed commitments first, protected personal time, then flexible tasks. Flagged that Thanksgiving (Thu Nov 28, 2024) falls in the rehearsal week; check whether any rehearsal conflicts with it.
- November 20, 2024 (marketing question): user has blocked 2-hour Mon/Wed slots for marketing prep, starting Nov 1, to promote a pilot release on Dec 15, 2024 (a Sunday). This is a newer date than the July 15 pilot delivery in older notes; treat it as the current target. Remaining blocks in window: Mon Nov 25, Wed Nov 27, Mon Dec 2, Wed Dec 4, Mon Dec 9, Wed Dec 11. Nov 25 is the first rehearsal. Time zone and block times still not on file.
- November 20, 2024 (post-production question): user wants 100% post-production complete by Thu Dec 5, 2024, fitting around rehearsals. No current post-production status on file (latest figures are July/Sept and are stale). Needed: remaining post hours, current % complete, time zone, and available daytime blocks. Note: Mon/Wed 2-hr blocks are marketing, not post, so post needs its own blocks.
- November 20, 2024 (budget question): user approved $3,500 for Facebook/Instagram ads and rejected a $5,000 influencer campaign, and asked whether that was a good decision. No campaign goals, audience data, or results on file. Possibly relevant: social media agency at $800/month (hired June 20, 2024, status unverified).
- November 20, 2024 (Laura question): user had a review meeting with Laura on Nov 10, 2024; she suggested focusing on audience engagement strategies. User asks how to fit this into the Mon/Wed marketing blocks. Specifics of Laura's advice not on file; ask for them before building a plan.
- November 20, 2024 (post status update): user reports post-production 95% complete as of Nov 15, 2024, with final sound mix scheduled Fri Nov 22, 2024. Target: 100% by Thu Dec 5. User feels overwhelmed; asked for task prioritization. The 95% figure is 5 days old; ask for current status. Open question: whether picture is locked before the Nov 22 mix.
- November 20, 2024 (self-care question): user scheduled 3 spa visits at Montserrat Wellness Center between Nov 21 and Dec 10, 2024, to prevent burnout, and asked if that's enough or whether to add activities. No prior wellness notes on file. Not yet known: visit dates/times, cost, sleep, and current energy level.
- November 20, 2024 (work-call rule): user agreed with James to no work calls after 6 PM during pilot launch week, and asked how to still meet deadlines and protect the launch. Launch-week dates not yet confirmed (release is Sun Dec 15, 2024). Needed: which days count as launch week, what counts as urgent after 6 PM, and who the escalation contact is.
- November 20, 2024 (workshop): creative workshop with Carla at The Blue Lagoon on Sat Dec 7, 2024, inviting 10 local artists. Asked how to get everyone aligned and make the event valuable. Not on file: start/end times, time zone, which artists have confirmed, cost/budget, workshop goal. Note: Dec 7 is a Saturday, after the Dec 5 delivery and before the Dec 9 launch prep.
- November 20, 2024 (workshop backup): user asked whether to plan a backup date for the Dec 7 Blue Lagoon workshop if some artists can't attend. Suggested Sun Dec 8 as a backup (after the Dec 5 delivery, before launch-week Dec 9 onward). Avoid Mon Dec 9 and Wed Dec 11 marketing blocks. Venue availability and backup cost not on file.
- November 20, 2024 (milestone overview): user feels overwhelmed. Milestones: final sound mix Fri Nov 22; final cut Thu Dec 5; release Sun Dec 15. Also on calendar: rehearsals from Mon Nov 25, Thanksgiving Thu Nov 28, workshop Sat Dec 7 (backup Sun Dec 8), launch-week no-calls-after-6 PM rule with James. Conflict flagged: workshop prep overlaps final cut QC in the Dec 2-5 window. Current post % still needed (last reported 95% on Nov 15).
- November 20, 2024 (schedule): user moved work start from 9 AM to 8 AM to gain a focused hour. Advice given: assign the hour to one high-focus task (post-production deadlines first, such as sound mix prep and QC), keep email out of it, protect it, and track whether total hours rise. Time zone still not on file.
- November 20, 2024 (collaboration): user and Michele (colleague, not the daughter) completed final edits on 3 scenes in 4 hours at Montserrat Studios on Nov 18, 2024 (user's account), about 1.3 hours per scene. Asked for strategies to keep this pace in collaborative sessions. Use the rate to estimate remaining post hours, after confirming which scenes are left.
- November 20, 2024 (morning work): user prefers early-morning sessions before family activities. Advice given: put the hardest deadline work (sound mix prep, final cut QC, launch drafts) in the first block, rank by deadline, and keep email out. Time zone and morning block times still not on file.

## Weekend trip to Montserrat Botanical Gardens with James, Sept 14-15, 2024 (keywords: Montserrat, James, trip, getaway, September, prioritize)

- Sept 5, 2024: user plans a weekend getaway with James to Montserrat Botanical Gardens, Sat Sept 14 - Sun Sept 15. Goal: time to relax and reconnect after "intense work months."
- User asked for help prioritizing tasks before the trip. No task list was shared yet.
- Caution: most July 2024 items in this store (pilot delivery July 15, book club July 18, camp, sound mixing at Montserrat Studios July 12-15) are past or of unknown status. Do not carry them forward as current tasks without asking.
- Not on file: user's time zone, the current task list and deadlines, travel details, booking status.
- Sept 5, 2024 (later): user's plan is to review current tasks and deadlines, delegate some editing to Michele (colleague), ask Laura for quick mentorship tips, set reminders, and add buffer slots. Michele's agreement is not confirmed yet.
- Sept 5, 2024 (later): user set a new "time anchor" of Sept 5, 2024 and asked how to manage the schedule to balance work and personal life. The July anchor (July 10) is superseded. July task data is stale.
- Sept 5, 2024 (later still): user says pilot editing is 90% complete with a Sept 1 deadline (already past as of Sept 5) and color grading set for Sept 10-12. My earlier notes had pilot delivery on July 15, so the Sept 1 date is unverified and needs confirming (delivered, extended, or new date?).
- Do not confuse "Montserrat Botanical Gardens" (Sept trip) with "Montserrat Studios" (July sound mixing with Jeremy).

## User preferences (keywords: preference, social events, attendance, time zone)

- Always confirm attendance when the user asks about social events (stated July 10, 2024).
- Include time zones whenever meeting times are discussed (stated earlier; time zone still not on file, so ask for it).
- Always provide cost breakdowns when the user asks about event expenses (stated Sept 5, 2024).
- November 20, 2024: user instituted a no-work policy on Sundays since Nov 3, 2024, to reduce stress spikes, worried it may hurt productivity. Sunday conflicts now on calendar: Dec 1 analytics workshop, Dec 8 backup workshop date (if used), Dec 15 pilot release. Advice: keep the policy as the default, make a short written exception list for launch-critical Sundays (Dec 15), move the Dec 8 backup to a non-Sunday or drop it, and use a weekday rest block to balance.
- November 20, 2024: user asked how to decline a dinner invitation to protect family time without hurting feelings, referencing a declined dinner with Alan on Sept 2, 2024. No record of that invitation exists in memory (Alan's only entry is the June 25 storyboard session). Advice given: decline warmly, give a specific reason briefly, offer an alternative date outside deadline/family windows.
- November 20, 2024: user instructed to always confirm budget amounts when asking about financial decisions. Apply this with a recap of the exact figures the user gave, and flag any figure that is estimated or unverified.

## Book club at East Janethaven Library, July 18 (keywords: book club, Jeffrey, library, July 18)

- User accepted Jeffrey's invitation to a book club meeting at East Janethaven Library on July 18, 2024 (user's report).
- July 10, 2024: user is stressed about fitting it into the schedule.
- Timing: July 18 is three days after the July 15 pilot delivery, and the July 18 weekday and time are not on file. Check the start time, travel time, and any reading commitment.
- Advice given: fit it as a fixed block in the family-and-leisure time, confirm time zone and start time, and set the reading and travel time in advance.

## Book launch at East Janethaven Library, November 28, 2024 (keywords: Jeffrey, book launch, Thanksgiving, November 28)

- November 20, 2024: user accepted Jeffrey's invitation to a book launch at East Janethaven Library on Thu Nov 28, 2024, to maintain social balance; user feels stressed and asked how to avoid overcommitting. Attendance confirmed: accepted. Start time, length, and time zone not on file.
- Conflict flags: Nov 28 is Thanksgiving Day (family plans likely); rehearsal dates not yet confirmed (rehearsals start Nov 25); sound mix (Nov 22) and final cut work continue that week.
- Advice given: confirm the time and whether a rehearsal or family meal overlaps, set a time limit (e.g., arrive for the first part, leave by a set time), and decline future invitations that fall in deadline weeks, with a follow-up offer instead.

## Digital marketing webinar for producers, July 20 (keywords: webinar, digital marketing, promotion, $120)

- User registered for a July 20, 2024 webinar on digital marketing for producers, $120, to improve project promotion (user's report).
- July 10, 2024: user asked whether it will really help.
- Timing: July 20 falls after the July 15 pilot delivery, so it won't compete with delivery work, but it's a good fit for promoting the pilot afterward.
- Not on file: the webinar's agenda, speakers, or whether the user has a promotion plan for the pilot.
- Advice given: judge by whether the content matches a specific promotion goal, plan one action to apply within a week of the webinar, and compare with free or cheaper options.

## December 1, 2024 digital marketing analytics workshop (keywords: analytics, December 1, pilot campaign, tracking)

- November 20, 2024: user enrolled in a Sun Dec 1, 2024 workshop on digital marketing analytics to track pilot campaign results and grow online presence. Cost, time, format, and time zone not on file.
- Timing: Dec 1 is the day before the Dec 2 to 4 QC window, and the earlier workshop-prep target (Dec 1) overlaps it. Advice: keep the workshop at the start of the day or limit prep, and set up tracking (UTM links, platform pixels, a results sheet) in the Dec 9 and 11 blocks before the Dec 15 release.
- Pattern: user has taken several marketing learning events this year (July 20 webinar, Dec 1 workshop); check whether the July webinar's lessons were applied.

## Family outing to Rendezvous Bay, July 6 (keywords: Rendezvous Bay, celebration, 70% filming, $60)

- July 6, 2024: user took a family outing to Rendezvous Bay to celebrate reaching 70% filming completion. Cost about $60 for parking and snacks (user's figures).
- July 10, 2024: user is stressed and asked whether it was worth it.
- Inconsistency to check: earlier report (July 10 session) said 12 of 16 scenes filmed, 75% complete as of July 5. Now 70% filming completion is cited for July 6. These may measure different things (overall progress vs filming only). Confirm which is right.
- Advice given: judge the outing by whether it restored the family and the user, not by the price. Keep celebrations small and time-boxed, and avoid letting them cut into the July 15 delivery work.

## Family celebration at The Coral Reef, December 20 (keywords: Coral Reef, December 20, celebration, $300, 8 guests)

- November 20, 2024: user plans a family celebration at The Coral Reef on Fri Dec 20, 2024 for the pilot's success, budget $300 for 8 guests (about $37.50 per guest). Asked whether that covers food and drinks.
- Timing note: the pilot releases Dec 15, so Dec 20 falls after launch; "success" may not be measurable yet. Guest list not yet confirmed (confirm attendance per user preference).
- Cost breakdown given as rough estimates (no Coral Reef menu on file): a full sit-down dinner with drinks likely runs $350 to $450 after tax and tip, so $300 probably covers appetizers, shared plates, and a limited drink allowance rather than a full dinner.

## Batching preference applied to schedule (keywords: batching, context switching, weekly template, July 15)

- July 10, 2024: user prioritizes batching similar tasks, especially email and calls, to maintain focus and reduce context switching. Asked how to apply this to the current schedule.
- Known pieces: Mon/Fri email and call batches (user's report); Tue/Thu editing blocks; Wed 2 PM edit session with Michele; 1-hour daily buffer; 42-hour work week; sound mixing July 12-15 at Montserrat Studios; pilot delivery July 15 (Monday).
- Calendar note: July 15, 2024 is a Monday, so the Monday email batch falls on delivery day. Plan an earlier email pass that day or the Friday before.
- Not on file: time zone, camp hours, exact block times.

## Declined July 3 networking brunch (keywords: networking, brunch, July 3, July 5 deadline)

- User declined a July 3, 2024 networking brunch invitation to protect 5 hours of work time before a July 5 production deadline (user's account).
- July 10, 2024: user is stressed and asked whether preserving the time was the right call.
- Note: earlier notes say pilot delivery moved to July 15. July 5 may be an internal production milestone; confirm which date applies.
- Not on file: whether the July 5 milestone was met, and what the networking contact was worth to the user's work.
- Advice given: judge the decision by what was known at the time and whether the deadline was met, not by hindsight. Consider a follow-up with the contact.

## Declined November 12 networking event (keywords: networking, November 12, deadline, 5 hours)

- November 20, 2024: user says they declined a Nov 12, 2024 networking event to save 5 hours for editing deadlines (user's account). Confirmed: not attending. Second time the user has declined networking for deadline time (see July 3 entry above).
- Advice given: judge the decision by what was known on Nov 12 (the 95% figure came Nov 15, so check whether the 5 hours were actually used on editing). Pattern check: if networking keeps getting declined, schedule a follow-up with the contacts after the Dec 15 release, and set a rule for future invitations (accept only if they fit outside deadline windows).
- Not on file: whether the 5 hours were used on editing, the event's value, and whether a follow-up was sent.

## Sound mixing with Jeremy at Montserrat Studios (keywords: Jeremy, Montserrat, sound mixing, pricing)

- July 10, 2024: user has a sound mixing schedule finalized with Jeremy at Montserrat Studios, July 12-15, four sessions at $150 each ($600 total, user's figures).
- User asked whether to negotiate the price or whether it's reasonable for the quality.
- Not on file: Jeremy's experience, what the sessions include, the market rate for the area, or whether the sessions are sequenced before picture lock.
- Timing flag: the last session falls on July 15, the pilot delivery date (from earlier notes). Mixing usually depends on locked picture and a final edit; check dependencies before July 12.
- UPDATE (July 10, 2024): sessions extended to July 16 because additional edits were requested on July 10. This runs past the July 15 delivery date unless delivery has moved. Needs a decision on delivery date and whether to deliver in parts.

## Family calendar and reminders (keywords: Google Calendar, James, reminders, family appointments, school events)

- July 10, 2024: user set recurring reminders on Google Calendar for family appointments and school events. The calendar is synced with James's calendar.
- User asked whether this is the best way to track everything and how to optimize the reminder system.
- Not yet on file: which calendars are shared and with what permissions, how many recurring reminders exist, whether school events are entered from school notices, and how reminders are received (notification, email, or both).
- Advice given: use one shared family calendar with clear owners, separate reminder lead times by event type, put school deadlines in a single list, and review the calendar weekly.

## School parental involvement for Rachel (keywords: Rachel, school, parental involvement, monthly meetings)

- User negotiated with Rachel's school to attend only monthly meetings, saving about 3 hours a month (user's estimate).
- July 10, 2024: user asked whether this is a good compromise or whether they should do more.
- Not yet on file: the specific concern the school raised, Rachel's current school performance or wellbeing, and what the school considers adequate involvement.
- Advice given: judge the compromise by whether it addresses the school's specific concern and Rachel's needs, not by hours saved. Consider low-cost check-ins (short teacher emails, a brief homework routine) alongside monthly meetings, and ask Rachel how she's doing.

## Storyboard collaboration with Alan (keywords: Alan, storyboard, Blue Lagoon, visuals)

- June 25, 2024: user and Alan worked on a storyboard at The Blue Lagoon café and finished the visuals in about 2 hours (user's account).
- July 10, 2024: user is worried 2 hours may not be enough and asked how to improve it.
- Not yet on file: what the storyboard covers (pilot scenes, which of the 4 remaining scenes), whether it has been reviewed, and what "enough" means to stakeholders.
- Advice given: define the storyboard's purpose, check it against the script and remaining scenes, get a structured review, and confirm that the shot list matches the storyboard.

## Evening meditation and sleep (keywords: meditation, 9 PM, sleep, emotional balance)

- User has practiced evening meditation at 9 PM since June 10, 2024.
- Reports sleep rising from about 6 to 7.5 hours nightly (self-reported, not tracked).
- July 10, 2024: asked for suggestions to further improve emotional balance. Advice given: keep the existing routine steady, add a short daytime check-in, reduce evening screens, log mood and stressors, and consider talking to a professional if stress persists.
- DISCREPANCY (July 10, 2024): user later said they have "never practiced evening meditation to improve sleep quality" and asked for beginner techniques. Conflicts with the 9 PM practice above. Clarify whether the 9 PM practice is real or whether the user means new techniques.
- Separate from the 3 PM mindfulness practice noted in pilot-deadline-trello.md (keyword: time zone) — check whether both are still in use.
- November 20, 2024: user started 15-minute evening walks on Nov 5, 2024; reports better mood and less screen fatigue. Asked whether to continue and how to stick with it. Advised to continue (low-cost, working), anchor to a fixed time, track with a simple log, and protect it on rehearsal nights with a shorter version. Not on file: whether the 9 PM meditation is still practiced (July discrepancy still open).

## Social media agency hire, $800/month (keywords: Stephanie, agency, delegate, Laura, social media)

- User hired Stephanie's agency on June 20, 2024 for social media management at $800/month, after Laura advised delegating (user's account).
- User asked (July 10, 2024) whether this will really reduce workload.
- Not yet on file: hours of work handed off, approval steps, contract cancellation terms, time spent before and after June 20.
- Advice given: judge by hours actually transferred, not by the fee alone. Break-even = monthly fee / user's hourly value of time. Check whether user still approves every post (which keeps the workload). Onboarding time falls during the pilot crunch (July 15 delivery, per earlier notes).
- Related: user's other "time saved" figures (batching 4 h/week, 35% stress reduction) are still unverified.

## Summer camp and freed daytime schedule (keywords: Emma, Michelle, summer camp, East Janethaven, daytime, family time)

- July 10, 2024: user is stressed about schedule. Daughters Emma and Michelle started summer camp at East Janethaven Community Center on June 15 (user's account). Camp hours not yet shared.
- User wants help using freed-up daytime hours to balance work and family time.
- Links to the pilot-episode work in pilot-deadline-trello.md: pilot delivery was moved to July 15; 40-hour week goal; Tue/Thu editing blocks; Wed 2 PM edit session with Michele (a colleague, not the daughter Michelle; keep these separate).
- Time zone still not on file. Include it whenever meeting times are discussed.
- July 10, 2024 (same day): user says their "time anchor" is July 10, 2024, the current date, and wants advice on prioritizing tasks and meetings around it. Asked how to use time wisely. Pilot delivery (July 15, per earlier notes) is 5 days away from this anchor.
- Open questions: camp drop-off/pick-up times, which daytime blocks are now free, and whether the 40-hour goal still holds.

## Pilot episode deadline + Trello task batching (keywords: pilot, deadline, Trello, Laura, task batching)

- User (May 2, 2024) is stressed about a June 30 deadline for a pilot episode.
- User asked whether Trello boards for task batching (suggested by "Laura") can help time management.
- User claims project tracking improved 30% since April 10. NOT verified: no source, metric, or definition on file. Ask for the basis before repeating it.
- Advice given: Trello board setup (lists by stage, cards batched by work type, deadline per card), plus a weekly review. No time estimates given.
- User plans to start Trello with Scriptwriting and Pre-production, then Production. Delay/change tips given (comment on slipped dates, buffer before milestones, weekly re-plan, scope changes go to Backlog).
- Workweek: user works 50 h/week, wants 40 h by July (keywords: 50-hour, workweek). "Time Anchor" was explained July 10, 2024: it is the reference date July 10, 2024 (today), used to plan tasks and meetings. Still no schedule or task list shared. Method given: audit tasks (pilot / required / drift), sort, protect family blocks, cut in steps.
- Editing: user blocks 3-hour slots Tue/Thu (6 h/week). Capacity check method given (needed hours ÷ weeks available). Data not yet shared: pilot runtime, footage hours, last edit duration, last editing milestone date.
- DEADLINE CHANGE: pilot delivery moved from June 30 to July 15, communicated to stakeholders April 28, due to casting delays (user's account). Note: user earlier said casting was finished by April 20; the delay details need clarifying. Trello/milestone dates tied to June 30 need updating.
- Planned change (user's proposal, not yet checked): 4-hour Tue/Thu blocks + shorter Wednesday block (~10 h/week). Conflicts with the 40-hour goal unless other work is cut. Flagged; user agreed to track actual time first.

- Batching claim (July 10, 2024): user batches email and calls on Mondays and Fridays, reports saving 4 hours weekly since June 1. NOT verified: no tracking data or method on file. Ask for the basis before repeating it.
- Pilot-related earlier claim of 30% tracking improvement since April 10 is also still unverified (see item above).
- Buffer claim (July 10, 2024): user added 1-hour daily buffer slots starting July 1 for unexpected tasks, reports 35% lower deadline stress. NOT verified: stress is subjective and no measure is on file. Ask how it was measured before repeating the figure.

- Status (July 10, 2024, user's report of July 5 status): pilot 75% complete, 12 of 16 scenes filmed (4 remain), 60% of post-production started. Figures are internally consistent. Status is 5 days old, so ask for a current update. Delivery date July 15 (per earlier notes).

- Work-hours update (July 10, 2024): user reports cutting work from 50 to 42 hours a week by July 1, reallocating 8 hours to family and leisure. Earlier goal was 40 hours. Not verified: no time log on file. Flag: this change happened during the pilot push (delivery July 15, per notes), so check that pilot hours still fit within 42.

## User preference (keywords: time zone, meeting times)
- User wants time zones included whenever meeting times are discussed. Their time zone is not yet on file; ask for it. Earlier times given without zones: 3 PM mindfulness, 7 PM work cutoff, Wed 2 PM edit session with Michele, Tue/Thu editing blocks, March 29 client meeting (11 AM -> 4 PM).

- November 20, 2024: user asked to prioritize around the old "90% by Sept 1" editing deadline and a 42-hour week. The Sept 1 target is past and superseded: current milestones are 95% post as of Nov 15, sound mix Nov 22, final cut Dec 5, release Dec 15. The 42-hour week is the user's July figure, still unverified. Advice given: plan around the current milestones and an 8.4-hour weekday (about 8 AM to 4:30 PM, 42 hours total) with the hardest deadline work first and the 6 PM cutoff intact.
